MSFT.rationale: MSFT presents a compelling fundamental case: revenue grew +18.3% YoY to $82.89B in Q3 FY2026, EPS grew +23.4% YoY, operating cash flow accelerated +26% YoY to $46.68B, and the balance sheet is fortress-grade with debt-to-equity of 0.12x and $78.27B cash vs $40.26B debt. The franchise is elite — Azure6  0% Azure growth, $37B AI ARR growing 123% YoY. Valuation has compressed to 28.5x trailing PE (bottom quartile of 25-43x one-year range) while fundamentals improved, creating a meaningful disconnect. However, several factors temper conviction: (1) QoQ EPS declined -17.2% despite revenue growth, suggesting Q2 may have been inflated by a non-recurring item; (2) the TTM is incomplete per the fiscal gap flag, making trailing earnings power imprecise; (3) $190B in 2026 capex creates genuine ROI uncertainty; (4) securities class actions targeting Copilot disclosures directly attack the AI narrative; (5) Xbox restructuring (64 cents lost per dollar invested) signals impairment risk. The July 29 earnings report is a credible near-term catalyst — if Azure hits 40-41% growth and management articulates AI ROI, the stock can re-rate. The earnings yield (3.5%) remains below the 10-year Treasury (4.57%), so the equity risk premium argument is weaker than the quant report implied, but 28.5x for 23% EPS growth is historically cheap for MSFT. Score of +0.35 reflects strong fundamentals and attractive valuation offset by capex uncertainty, legal overhang, and incomplete TTM precision.

sources_cited.excerpt: Copilot is the newest brand bet: AI embedded into every Microsoft product at $30 per user per month. If Copilot achieves 30% attach rate among Microsoft 365's 400M subscribers, it adds $36B in annual revenue at near-100% incremental margins.
Cloud revenue now represents 65% of total revenue, up from 50% in 2023.
Record revenue of $281.7 billion (up 15%) and operating income of $128.5 billion.
Microsoft ended a planned $3 billion cloud infrastructure collaboration with Oracle after failing to obtain FedRAMP security certification.
US lawmakers have heightened scrutiny over Microsoft's sales of OpenAI-powered AI services to Chinese technology firms via its Azure platform.

Microsoft is developing its own proprietary AI models (MAI) to reduce reliance on OpenAI and Anthropic… unveiled seven MAI models in June 2026, including MAI-Thinking-1, which matches Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 on coding tasks.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma stated the gaming business is 'not healthy,' losing 64 cents for every dollar invested.
Azure growth likely reaching 40-41% in constant currency, slightly above Microsoft's 39-40% guidance.
